steps.text: In medium saucepan, combine sugar, flour, cornstarch and salt and whisk to combine. In a medium bowl, whisk milk and egg yolks until smooth. Gradually stir into sugar mixture. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and comes to a full boil. Boil and stir for one minute.
Remove from heat and stir in chocolate, butter, and vanilla. Stir until melted.
Pour into pie shell. Place plastic wrap over filling to prevent skin from forming and chill for several hours. Top with meringue or whipped cream and chocolate curls if so desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Fudgy Chocolate Cream Pie
raw_recipe.description: This no-bake pie is a family favorite, and it's so easy to make. You can also top it with meringue and pop it in the oven, or simply serve it chilled with whipped cream and chocolate curls.
raw_recipe.name: Fudgy Chocolate Cream Pie

review.reviewBody: This was excellent! I added extra 2 tsp. cornstarch and 1/2 c. milk to make enough to fill pie. Another reviewer said it was very thick. So by using just a bit more cornstarch and extra milk it was perfect and cut really neat slices. Cornstarch is unique in the way that when you bring to a hard boil; than boil for 1 min longer the filling is perfect. If you overcook it, it will go back to thin!!!I made this for my coffee group and they gave it 10 stars!

I made this for Thanksgiving 2013 and I loved this recipe for fudgy chocolate pie! that is exactly what it is fudgy and good! this recipe will fill a regular 9 inch pie crust but, if you want it a little more full, which I did, then take the advice of other reviewers and add a 1/2 a cup more of milk and 2 extra tablespoons of cornstarch that's what I did and it fills pie crust better if you want to fill a deep dish pie then double the recipe. I added the chocolate at the beginning to let it melt while filling was cooking and I had some scary moments, first I was stirring this filling with a spoon and the chocolate was not incorporating into the rest of the mixture it was melting but it was a mottled mess, thought it was ruined, at least it was visually, it looked bad!! so I got out my whisk and whisked it quickly as the mixture was thickening and when I did that everything smoothed out and blended just fine, I would not use a spoon, use a wire whisk.

This was delicious. I added the extra half cup of milk and cornstarch as others suggested. Might decrease the sugar a little next time. I also heated the milk partially in the microwave (a little over a minute) to decrease cooking time, and used a double boiler so as not to overcook. Overall a winner!

I made the pie according to the directions, but did also increase the corn starch by 2 tsp. and the milk by 1/2 cup, as several cooks suggested. The quantity that resulted was the perfect amount for a 9" pie shell. The directions do not mention how long to stir, and for those of you who will make this pie in the future, you will be stirring constantly for at least 15 to 19 minutes, before the filling gets thick. It is important to stir constantly as the filling could burn. The flavor was a delicious chocolate flavor, and I topped the pie with whipped cream and chocolate shavings. I hope you all will try this pie; you will not be disappointed.

I've been craving chocolate cream pie something fierce this week, so I decided to give this recipe a go. It was super easy to make, and it turned out great! It's still cooling in the fridge right now, but I got impatient and had a slice already, and even slightly warm, it set up beautifully and tasted really rich and chocolatey. I did take the suggestion to add 2 tsp of corn starch and another 1/2 cup milk, because my pie dish is very deep, and that seems to be a good amount of filling - enough to make a good balance with a whipped cream topping. I also used the suggestion of spraying and wiping down my plastic wrap before covering the pie, and it made it much easier to peel away. I will definitely be making this again next time I need to bring a dessert for something!

Not bad but my mum's recipe is better! :P
Also--what in the heck--there is no explanation on how to make the meringue topping! I had to search on Allrecipes for one that explained that because I've never made a meringue pie topping before, just regular meringues! So if you got stuck like I did search on allrecipes for 
"Chocolate Meringue Pie" and read the instructions in the second half of the recipe about how to make the topping. Also be verrry careful when you are stirring the chocolate pie filling on high heat. I hate how recipes like these say "boil" because even though it may be at boiling temperatures, it's not water, and you won't see the bubbling on the surface. The mixture will be burning on the bottom if you do see bubbles somehow, so make sure to watch it carefully. As soon as it starts to feel "thick" and resists you stirring it, immediately turn down the heat or turn it off completely. The residual heat may be enough to finish cooking it, especially if you've added sufficient cornstarch. Also if you don't have semi sweet chocolate, you can make your own homemade by using 1 tablespoon of butter + 3 tablespoons cocoa powder for each 1 oz of semi sweet chocolate. Melt the butter first in a measuring cup then mix in the cocoa powder, then add this combo to the egg and sugar mixture on the stove. Work quickly or it will burn! My first try had a few little lumps in it, probably from too high heat.

Good luck in the kitchen!

This was my first cream pie! Everyone approved. It wasn't too sweet for me at all, and I would definitely make it again. 

I only made a few changes. I replaced the unsweetened chocolate with 3 tbsp of cocoa powder and 1 tbsp of butter. Melt the butter and then mix in the cocoa powder to avoid lumps.

I made a meringue topping by whisking 3 egg whites until foamy, then adding 6 tbsp of sugar. I continued beating until stiff peaks formed and then added 1/2 tsp vanilla. Lastly, I baked at 325 degrees for 15 minutes.

Turned out great!

Lives up to it's name... this is a thick, rich, chocolate "fudgy" pie. Absolutely delicious! only variations I made was using half & half in place of reg. milk (makes for a smoother, richer pie)... & also combined the flour & cornstarch together in a cup, added just enough water to make a thin paste, then added this to the liquid mixture of milk/eggs. This eliminated any lumps. I used the Basic Flaky Pie Crust recipe off of this site & it balanced out the sweetness of the filling really well. Be forewarned: this is a thick, rich pie... but in my opinion, with the homemade pie crust, it wasn't too sweet... and oh, so good when you're craving something chocolatey! This is definitely a keeper!
Edited to add: this is my "go to" recipe now for chocolate pie! I've made it dozens of times & have found that we like it best with a regular egg white meringue topping. I also use canned milk when out of half & half and it's just as good! (Carnation, NOT condensed) If you're in a hurry, skip the homemade crust & use the Pillsbury pie crusts that you simply roll out.

After reading the reviews, I decided to make the changes several people had mentioned. I added the x-tra 2 tsp of cornstarch and increased the milk by 1/2 cup. I topped it off with some homemade whipped cream and some shaved chocolate. It was amazing! and its very easy to make, the only thing is that you have to CONSTANTLY! keep stirring! I walked away from the stove for a minute and my chocolate filling almost burned. It takes about 13-15min for the pie filling to get thick. I timed it! LOL!

This was honestly the best chocolate pie I have ever had--and I had the pleasure of making it. I too, would recommend the extra tsp of cornstarch and 1/2 cup of milk, because it ended up working out very well. Also, don't be worried if the mixture begins to clump up, when boiled. It is perfectly normal, just make sure you try to squash the larger ones. Thats really all I would recommend you doing apart from the general directions. I really loved this pie. Me and my sister secretly licked the entire pan clean after we poured it into the pie shell. :)

Perfectly easy and delicious! I took the advice of other reviewers and increased the milk to two cups and added to additional tablespoons of cornstarch. What a chocolate flavor! I topped my pie with meringue because I didn't have whipping cream or whipped topping in the house. This is going in my permanent recipe file.We recently had a group of men from our church over for lunch. As they were eating this pie, I heard things like " the texture is absolutely perfect", " so creamy", certainly not the usual man talk! This is my permanent go to chocolate pie recipe!

I have made this recipe at Holidays for the last two years. Year one, with my grandmother's double boiler, and strictly by the recipe. Perfect. This year I went rogue, adding a T of chocolate powder, and using whole milk only as a general cooking nite. Then today, I made two more with the same adjustments, amd used 1 T cornstarch and 2T self rising flour. Still perfect and delicious.

I made this with arrowroot instead of cornstarch because we didn't have cornstarch. Turned out perfectly, and love the flavor. Everyone chose it over the other two pies the first night and like that it was gone. Am making another today (2 days later). I made homemade whipped cream for it it as well instead of meringue
Perfect amount of sweetness. Easy to make and very delicious

Used a premade deep dish crust from ALDI, and topped with whipped cream just before serving. It was a HUGE hit - I have to say it is incredibly rich (hence the "fudgy"), I couldn't finish my piece as a dessert shortly after a meal, but now I know to wait much longer, :)
I thought this turned out really good!! It was creamy and light. I put ghram cracker crumbs on it.

Really lovely recipe. Easy and quick if you already have the pie crust made. The first time I used this recipe it was the base for a coconut cream pie. Then my mother asked for just the chocolate pie. Yum! I used heavy cream in place of milk as that was all I had. Also used dark chocolate. So good!

I posted my pie on the meringue II site also. I made the changes as suggested and I had enough filling for my pie. This will be one of my favorite pies to make! It looks so pretty. And my family loves it.
Updating my review. I forgot to add that I added 2 extra teaspoons of cornstarch. Also, an extra half cup of milk. Super delicious!
